environment.ffmpeg: vendored 7.1.1 (accepts -filter_complex_script with a deprecation warning); CI Linux uses Ubuntu's apt FFmpeg

objective: Replace frame-sized animation filter chains with bounded compilation
flags: Compiler v2 on; YAMAKAN_ANIMATION_COMPILER=1 selects the per-frame compiler (v1) for new plans
deviations: Bounded segments of the per-frame samples (explicit tolerances: opacity 1/255, volume 1/200), not analytic piecewise curves; every frame stays within half a tolerance of v1
Key values outside opacity 0-1 or volume 0-16, which rendered before, are refused under either compiler; overshoot between keys is clamped
Transform animation channels, previously stored and silently ignored, are refused before preview/export (CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE) until transform animation is built

The filter graph (and the loudness measure pass's) is written to a script file passed by absolute path, so long graphs no longer meet the command-line limit; core/render.ts change recorded in imports.json
Render startup/RSS was not measured as a separate benchmark; graph size is asserted instead (a ten-minute ramp: at most 256 segments instead of 18,000)

tests.result: 9 animation-complexity tests: v2 within half a tolerance of v1 on every frame (holds, steps, linear, Bezier, ends; 30 and 24000/1001); graph size bounded (ten-minute ramp <=256 vs 18,000; +6 dB volume ramp <=400); rendered video and audio follow the curve, steps and ends with a bounded graph; the two-key windowed sampler equals whole-channel sampling on random curves and edge cases; windows match the export's frames; v1 selectable and tolerances pinned to the version; duplicate keys, out-of-range and non-finite values, transform channels, per-channel and per-plan budgets refused; empty channels draw nothing. jobs.test.ts finds FFmpeg by its workspace (the graph is now a file)
